title: 2100 Bioanalyzer Operation for PCR, GTP and IVT Products
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science

steps_raw.instruction: 2100 Bioanalyzer Operation for Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), Genotyping (GTP) and In Vitro Transcription (IVT) Products

Scope and Applicability: The Agilent Bioanalyzer is used as a quality control step for PCR and IVT products. Peak size, shape, and sample concentration are recorded and used to evaluate samples on a pass/fail level.
1.0 µl of 1:2 diluted PCR product stored at -20ºC, 1.0 µl of GTP product stored at 4ºC, or 1.0 µl of IVT product stored at -80°C.
For PCR/GTP (all included in Agilent DNA 7500 LabChip kit Agilent 5607-1506)
DNA 7500 Marker DNA Dye Concentrate.
For IVT (all included in Agilent RNA 6000 Nano LabChip kit Agilent 5607-1511)
RNA Nano Dye Concentrate.
RNA 6000 Nano Marker.
RNA 6000 Nano Gel Matrix.
RNA 600 Nano LabChip.
0.5 ml epi-tube with locking cap
Nuclease-free water (Applied Biosystems AM9932).
Electrode cleaner chips (included in all LabChip kits)
Filter pipette tips (Rainin # GP-L10F, GP-L200F, GP-L1000F)
0.65 ml Eppendorf tubes
PCR mat for 96 well plates
Chip priming station (Agilent 5065-4401)
Microcentrifuge (Eppendorf 5417 C or equivalent)
Benchtop centrifuge (e.g. Eppendorf 5810 R) with microplate carriers
Rainin Pipetteman (p2, p10, p200, p1000, p20 repeater).
Dye contains DMSO, avoid contact with skin.
Electropherogram and gel picture of PCR or IVT product, concentration and size in a file with extension .xad.

Warning: This protocol is extremely sensitive to RNase contamination; ensure that you have been properly trained using sterile techniques before starting this protocol. Personal Protective Equipment () should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.

NOTE: Unless otherwise noted, ‘spin down’ means to spin the tubes in a microcentrifuge for 5-10” at top speed (or plates in a bench-top centrifuge 2’ at 1800rpm) in order to drive the liquid to the bottom of the tubes/wells.
PCR/GTP Assay: DNA 7500
Prepare gel and samples for PCR/GTP assay:
Allow DNA dye concentrate (blue vial) and DNA gel matrix (red vial) to equilibrate to room temperature for 30 min.
Protect dye concentrate from light.
Vortex DNA dye concentrate and add 25 µl to DNA gel matrix tube.
Vortex solution, spin down, and transfer to DNA 7500 spin filter.
Centrifuge at 4000 g for 10 min. Protect solution from light. Store at 4°C in “DNA BA” box. Use within 4 weeks.
Obtain tracking sheet – this indicates which PCR samples to run.
Thaw PCR or GTP plate at RT for 3’, spin down. Replace plate seal with rubber mat as lid.
Clean the bioanalyzer electrodes:
Pipette 350 µl of NFdH2O into a labeled electrode cleaner chip. Make sure it spreads to all corners of the wells.
Place the filled electrode cleaner chip inside the bioanalyzer and close the lid. Check that Bioanalyzer software acknowledges the presence of a chip.
Wait 10 seconds, and open the lid.
Remove the cleaner chip and wait 10 seconds for the water on the electrodes to evaporate.
Close the bioanalyzer lid.
Methodology/Procedures:
This protocol is meant for 12 samples for PCR/GTP assay.
Allow the filtered gel-dye mix to come to room temperature, protected from light, for 30 minutes before use.
Make sure the chip priming station base plate is set at position “C” and the plunger is in topmost position.
Label a new DNA 7500 chip with the sample information and run number (eg. 6/21, 08, A). Record run name on tracking sheet– “BA_date_Run#_PCR(or GTP). Flip chip counter to number of next chip.
Add 9.0 µl gel dye mix to the well marked with a “G”.
Place chip in priming station. Close the chip priming station and press the plunger until the clip holds it.
Wait exactly 30 seconds, and release the clip.
Wait 5 seconds for the plunger to rise, and slowly pull it up to the 1ml position.
Open the chip priming station and check the underside of the chip that the capillaries are no longer visible.
If there are any visible, repeat steps 8.5 through 8.7. If capillaries are still visible start over with a new chip.
Add 9.0 µl gel-dye mix to each of the other two wells marked “G”.
Add 5 µl DNA 7500 marker (green vial) to ladder well and 12 samples wells. Add 1.0 µl DNA 7500 Ladder (yellow vial) to the well marked with a picture of a ladder.
Add 1.0 µl of sample (diluted PCR product or GTP product) into each of the sample wells. Change tips between each sample.
Place the chip in the IKA Vortex Mixer and vortex at 2200 rpm for exactly 1 minute.
Run the bioanalyzer and software:
Run the chip in the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer within 5 minutes of loading.
Open the 2100 Expert program on the bioanalyzer computer.
Place the loaded chip inside the bioanalyzer and close the lid.
If it is not already selected, click on “Instrument” on the left side of the screen.
On the right of the screen, select “DNA 7500 Series II” for the Assay Selection (click “Assay…,” then “dsDNA,” and select “DNA 7500 Series II”).

In the field marked “File Prefix,” after “BA_” type in “BA_YYMMDD_NN_PCR” where YY=year, MM=month, DD=day, and NN=the number of the bioanalyzer run of the day (e.g. the fifth run of the day would be “05”).
Click the “Start” button.
Once the assay starts, click on “Data” on the left side of the screen.

Click the “Chip Summary” tab and enter the sample information for each of the 12 samples in the format “PCR_YYMMDD_PP_RCC” (or “GTP_YYMMDD_PP_RCC”) where YYMMDD=date of the sample plate, PP=sample plate number, R=sample row from sample plate, and CC=sample column from sample plate.
Electronic gel pictures and electropherograms of the ladder and samples may be viewed by clicking on the “Gel” and “Electropherogram” tabs, respectively.
Run will take approximately 30 minutes.
Remove the LabChip from the bioanalyzer and dispose it once the run has completed.
Clean the electrodes with the electrode cleaner as described in steps 7.7 through 7.11.
Empty the electrode cleaner chip at the end of the day.
Technical Information:
When pipetting samples into the LabChips, insert the pipette tip to the bottom of the well to prevent the formation of bubbles.
Protect the dye and dye mixtures from light to prevent decomposition.
Clean the electrodes before the first run of the day, between each bioanalyzer run, and after last run of day.
Use a new electrode cleaner chip with each new LabChip Kit.
Sample wells must all contain 5.0 µl, or assay will not run.
Do not touch the bioanalyzer during an assay.
Electrode cleaner chips should not be filled more than 350 µl, or electrodes may malfunction.
Prepare gel for IVT assay:
Allow RNA gel matrix (red vial) to equilibrate to room temperature for 30 min.
Pipette 550 µl of RNA 6000 Nano gel mix (red vial) into an RNA 6000 spin filter.
Centrifuge at 4000 g for 10 minutes.
Aliquot 65 µl (enough for two LabChips) of filtered gel into 0.5 ml RNase-free microfuge tubes. Write “gel” and the date on tubes. Use filtered gel within 4 weeks. Store at 4°C in “RNA BA” box.
Prepare ladder for IVT assay:
Take out two Nano Reagents Part II boxes from the MB5 -20°C freezer, thaw at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Vortex and transfer contents (35 µl each) into two 0.65 ml tubes.
Heat denature at 70°C for 2 minutes. Immediately transfer to bench-top cooler for 5 minutes.
Dispense 2.2 µl into 0.65 ml tubes with single-channel P20 repeater.
Label with date, as “L, date”.
Store at -80°C in “RNA ladder aliquot” box until ready for use. One aliquot is enough for two LabChips.
Clean the bioanalyzer electrodes:
Pipette 350 µl of NFdH2O water into a labeled electrode cleaner chip.
Place the water chip inside the bioanalyzer and close the lid. Check that the Bioanalyzer software acknowledges the presence of a chip.
Wait 1 minute, and open the lid.
Remove the chip and wait 10 seconds for the water on the electrodes to evaporate.
Close the bioanalyzer lid.
Methodology: This protocol is meant for 12 samples of IVT assay. Prepare the gel-dye mix:
Allow the RNA 6000 Nano dye concentrate (blue vial) and RNA gel aliquot to come to room temperature for 30 minutes.
Protect dye concentrate from light.
Vortex the dye concentrate for 10 seconds, spin down.
Add 1.0 µl dye concentrate to 65 µl aliquot of filtered gel. Using a blue sharpie, write the date on the top of the lid to indicate that dye has been added.
Vortex and spin tube at 13000 for 10 minutes at room temperature. Protect from light.
Obtain tracking sheet – this indicates which IVT samples to run.
Thaw the IVT plate from -80°C at room temperature for about 3 minutes. Spin down.
Remove plate seal and cover with a 96-well rubber mat.

Denature for 5 minutes at 70°C in thermocycler with no heated lid. After denaturing, place on ice for a full 5 minutes, then spin down. During BA chip loading, the plate can remain on ice or on the bench-top cooler.
This step is critical to keep the product ‘snapped’ in position after the sample has been denatured.
Initial and date side of plate to indicate it has been denatured.
Pull ladder aliquot from -80°C freezer and keep in bench-top cooler until ready for use.
Load the gel-dye mix and samples:
Label a new RNA chip with the sample information and run number (eg. 6/21, 08, H).
Make sure the chip priming station base plate is set at position “C” and plunger is in the topmost position.
Add 9.0uL gel dye mix to the well marked with a “G”.
Place chip in priming station.
Close the chip priming station and press the plunger until the clip holds it.
Wait exactly 30 seconds, and release the clip.
Wait 5 seconds for the plunger to rise, and slowly pull it up to the 1mL position.
Open the chip priming station and check the underside of the chip that the capillaries are no longer visible.
If there are any visible, repeat steps 12.11 through 12.14. If the capillaries remain visible start over with a new chip.
Add 9.0 µl gel-dye mix to each of the two wells marked “G.”
Add 5.0 µl RNA 6000 marker (green vial) in the ladder well and 12 sample wells.
Add 1.0 µl RNA 6000 ladder to the well marked with a picture of a ladder.
Add 1.0 µl of denatured IVT sample into each of the sample wells. Change tips between each sample.
Place the chip in the IKA Vortex Mixer and vortex at 2200 rpm for exactly 1 minute.
Run the bioanalyzer and software:
Run the chip in the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer within 5 minutes of loading.
Open the 2100 Expert program on the bioanalyzer computer.
Place the loaded chip inside the bioanalyzer and close the lid.
If it is not already selected, click on “Instrument” on the left side of the screen.
On the right of the screen, select “Eukaryote Total RNA Nano Series II” for the Assay Selection (click “Assay…,” then “RNA,” and select “Eukaryote Total RNA Nano Series II.”)

In the field marked “File Prefix,” after “BA_” type in “BA_YYMMDD_NN_IVT” where YY=year, MM=month, DD=day, and NN=the number of the bioanalyzer run of the day (e.g. the fifth run of the day would be “05”). Record run name on “PCR to IVT” coversheet – “BA_date_Run#_IVT. Flip chip counter to number of next chip.
Click the “Start” button.
Once the assay starts, click on “Data” on the left side of the screen, then “Chip Summary” tab.

Enter the sample information for each of the 12 samples in the format “IVT_YYMMDD_PP_RCC” where YYMMDD=date of the sample plate, PP=sample plate number, R=sample row from sample plate, and CC=sample column from sample plate.
Electronic gel pictures and electropherograms of the ladder and samples may be viewed by clicking on the “Gel” and “Electropherogram” tabs, respectively.
Remove the LabChip from the bioanalyzer and dispose of it once the run has completed.
Clean the electrodes with the electrode cleaner as described in steps 11.16 through 11.20.
Empty the electrode cleaner chips at the end of the day.
Technical Information:
When pipetting samples into the LabChips, insert the pipette tip to the bottom of the well to prevent the formation of bubbles.
Protect the dye and dye mixtures from light to prevent decomposition.
RNA gel-dye mix must be made fresh on the day of the run. If unused, throw it away.
Clean the electrodes before the first run of the day, between each bioanalyzer run, and after the last run of the day.
Use a new electrode cleaner chip with each new LabChip Kit.
Sample wells must all contain 5.0 µl, or assay will not run.
Do not touch the bioanalyzer during an assay.
Electrode cleaner chips should not be filled more than 350 µl, or electrodes may malfunction.
RNA ladder and samples must be denatured at 70°C to avoid gel mobility errors from secondary structure.
